transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for this pre-purchase review. As you know, we're considering a vendor's indoor-air-quality monitoring system for the science wing. The preliminary discussion has focused on the six-monitor package at $3,100, though the vendor also offers a nine-monitor package at $4,320. Before I record my approval, I'd like to hear from each of you — facilities, business office, and our school nurse — on any findings or concerns relevant to this purchase. Let's start with facilities. What can you tell me?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. I completed an inspection of the science wing this week, and I found that there are nine separate classrooms that each need a monitor because they have separate ventilation zones. The six-monitor package we've been discussing won't be sufficient — we'd actually need the nine-monitor package to cover every room. I haven't yet entered the room-by-room report into the purchasing worksheet, but the inspection findings are clear.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I can speak to the funding side of this. I verified the ledger this week, and a restricted capital account has exactly enough approved funding to cover the $4,320 nine-monitor package — no general-fund transfer would be needed. I should note that the formal finance memo is still awaiting this pre-purchase review before it's finalized.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I'd like to share my findings from the health side. I reviewed the student health plans this week, and the monitors' alerts must be set at 1,000 ppm carbon dioxide and reviewed by me weekly during the first quarter after installation. I've completed that review, but I should note that I haven't yet added these health settings to the implementation plan. We'll need to make sure those alert thresholds and the weekly review schedule are incorporated before this moves forward.
transcript.speaker: A4
